anomalies.observed: U14 pin 5, named ~{RESET}, is directly connected to the GND net. In contrast, U13 pin 5 is pulled up to SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V through R18.
anomalies.expected: The SC16IS752 reset input is active low and should be deasserted (pulled high or driven by a controlled reset signal), not tied to ground, especially because U14 is otherwise connected to the SPI bus and to serial connectors J17/J18.
anomalies.impact: U14 is held in reset and cannot operate. The second UART expansion controller and its serial ports (RX3/TX3/RX4/TX4) will be nonfunctional, and the SPI bus will see an unresponsive slave.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of LEDs D4, D14, and D23. No 3.3 V source, buffer output, switch, or other driver is attached to this net.
anomalies.expected: A net named /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW should be a switched 3.3 V LED supply so that the connected LED anodes receive power; otherwise the LEDs cannot light.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 will remain off because their common anode supply net is floating. This removes the intended status/Ethernet/PI-activity indications associated with those LEDs.

parsed.summary: The design files contain at least one clear anomaly: U14's active-low reset pin is tied to GND, disabling the second SC16IS752 UART controller despite its SPI and serial connections. A second likely issue is the floating /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW net, which supplies only LED anodes and has no connected 3.3 V source.
